audited: smart-comfyui-gallery @ branch frontend-typescript, working tree as of 2026-08-25. First-party Python and TypeScript under db/, metaparse/, sg_web/, sglint/, story_renderers/, vision/, tests/, benchmarks/, frontend/src/. Excluded: .venv, node_modules, vendor, sg_web/static/build, sg_web/static/*.min.js, frontend/src/generated/api.d.ts (generated), and the verbatim schema DDL text embedded in db/migrate.py. Audited for improper variable usage only: magic numbers, magic strings, duplicated constants, and hardcoded values that should be named or derived. Every reported literal was opened and read at the cited line.

findings.literal: WHEN 'subsecond' THEN 0 WHEN 'second' THEN 1 WHEN 'minute' THEN 60 WHEN 'hour' THEN 3600
findings.concept: the granule->seconds table, restated as a SQL CASE
findings.evidence: db/when.py:526-534 SPAN is the declared single table: subsecond 0.001, second 1.0, minute 60.0, hour 3600.0, day 86400.0, month 2_629_746, year 31_556_952, decade 315_569_520. This CASE gives subsecond 0 (not 0.001) and, per db/facets.py:150, collapses EVERY coarse precision to 2147483647. db/pages.py:1359-1361 _FINE_ENOUGH admits 'decade', 'year' and 'month' as real precisions, and db/facets.py:139-143's own comment says `lte:<bin width>` is exactly 'fine enough for this bin' -- so a decade-precision claim (315_569_520 s per when.SPAN) tests as 2147483647 and is excluded from every bin narrower than INT_MAX, which is every bin. Same word, two tables, and the second one lost three rungs.
findings.fix: Generate the CASE arms from when.SPAN at import time (a module-level f-string joining `WHEN '<name>' THEN <int(seconds)>` over when.SPAN), so a rung added to when.SPAN cannot be missing here. Name it db/facets.py GRANULE_SECONDS_SQL.

findings.concept: the coarse-precision fallback in the granule CASE
findings.evidence: Continuation of db/facets.py:149. 2147483647 is INT32_MAX standing in for 'coarser than a day', but db/when.py:526-528 has real seconds for month, year and decade and db/pages.py:1359 relies on them. No comment derives 2147483647.
findings.fix: Replace with generated arms for month/year/decade from when.SPAN; keep a named `_UNKNOWN_GRANULE` only for a precision the table does not contain.

findings.concept: the ceiling on rows one ledger read returns
findings.evidence: db/ledger.py:59 declares `PAGE_MOST = 2_000` as 'Most rows one read returns'. Line 375 retypes the number instead, so raising PAGE_MOST silently leaves the item pager behind.

findings.concept: the time-basis vocabulary
findings.evidence: db/context.py:58 declares TIME_BASES = ("capture", "embedded", "filename", "folder", "btime", "mtime", "first_seen") -- SEVEN members. This copy has six: 'first_seen' is missing. The docstring above it (db/planning.py:1143-1144) claims it is "the time bases a file occurrence may rest on (db/schema.sql derived_media_occurrence.basis)", and db/migrate.py:3512 shows that CHECK does include 'first_seen'. tests/needs.py:85 and tests/test_the_corpus_spans_the_shape.py:141 gate context.TIME_BASES only; nothing holds _BASES against it.

findings.concept: SQL bound-parameter batch size for an IN clause
findings.evidence: The same concept -- how many ids fit in one `... IN (?,?,...)` -- is 500 at db/evolution.py:131, db/prompts.py:190, db/prompts.py:371, db/retrieval.py:374 and db/runner.py:929. Upstream fixes the real ceiling: ../refs/sqlite/sqlite/src/sqliteLimit.h:189-191 defines SQLITE_MAX_VARIABLE_NUMBER as 32766 at the commit db/connect.py:174 already cites (sqlite/sqlite@b09c88c14). Neither 900 nor 500 is that number, a fraction of it, or derived from anything else stated in the repo, and nothing says why the scan path may use 900 while five others may not.
findings.fix: One module-level `PARAM_BATCH` in db/connect.py beside the other per-connection facts, derived from the limit the driver reports (`getlimit(sqlite3.SQLITE_LIMIT_VARIABLE_NUMBER)`, whose compile-time default is ../refs/sqlite/sqlite/src/sqliteLimit.h:190) with a documented margin. Every call site reads it.

findings.concept: SQL bound-parameter batch size, restated as the slice bound

findings.concept: a year in seconds, as the zoom ladder's week-bin ceiling

findings.concept: a ledger page size
findings.evidence: Instances: db/inspecting.py:342 (events), db/inspecting.py:360 (events_before), db/ledger.py:142 (latest). Three functions over the same table with the same unnamed page size, while the same pair of modules already names the CEILING (db/ledger.py:59 PAGE_MOST = 2_000). The default is unnamed; the maximum is named.
findings.fix: `PAGE_DEFAULT = 500` in db/ledger.py beside PAGE_MOST; all three signatures read it.

findings.concept: the thresholds of a duration-spelling ladder
findings.evidence: Five independent duration formatters exist, each with its own thresholds and units: db/when.py:726-730 (_hours), sg_web/console.py:28-33 (_seconds), sg_web/timeline_view.py:641-646 (_lasted), story_renderers/formatting.py:88-96 (duration), frontend/src/operations.ts:81-86 (seconds). frontend/src/operations.ts:83-85 is a line-for-line transcription of sg_web/console.py:29-33 in another language, with no gate holding them together. story_renderers/formatting.py:1-2 claims spelling is 'decided once, here'.
findings.fix: One ladder per audience, named: keep story_renderers/formatting.py `duration` as the human ladder and sg_web/console.py `_seconds` as the operator ladder, delete db/when.py `_hours` and sg_web/timeline_view.py `_lasted`, and emit the operator ladder's thresholds to the client instead of retyping them in frontend/src/operations.ts.

findings.concept: rounding an instant down to its day bin
findings.evidence: Same shape as the five hour-bin copies (see sg_web/media_view.py:905), with 86400 typed three times on one line. db/pages.py:1337 already holds the day width as int(when.DAY).
findings.fix: Same helper, parameterised by bin name: `window_for("day", moment)`.

findings.concept: rounding an instant down to its hour bin
findings.evidence: The identical expression pair (`int(x // 3600) * 3600` and `... + 3600`) beside `{"bin": "hour", ...}` at sg_web/media_view.py:905, sg_web/person_view.py:99, sg_web/story_view.py:43, sg_web/story_view.py:44 and sg_web/timeline_view.py:112. Five hand-written copies of one function, with sg_web/media_view.py:888 a sixth in the day flavour. db/pages.py:1333-1340 BINS already holds the widths these round to.
findings.fix: One helper -- `hour_window(start, end)` in sg_web/timeline_view.py, reading its width from pages.BINS['hour'] -- called by the four other sites.

findings.concept: an hour in seconds, in a test fixture
findings.evidence: Declared identically at tests/test_a_camera_day_is_a_story.py:31, tests/test_a_media_context_is_one_interpretation.py:31, tests/test_a_prompt_is_a_reusable_semantic_substrate.py:52, tests/test_a_story_plan_is_structure_from_frozen_evidence.py:54, tests/test_a_story_render_words_only_what_the_plan_claims.py:30, tests/test_an_evolution_is_a_view_of_a_plan.py:31, tests/test_events_are_grouping_hypotheses.py:29, tests/test_every_file_has_a_when.py:30, tests/test_something_runs_without_being_asked.py:29, tests/test_the_timeline_is_a_surface.py:29, tests/test_time_is_a_corroboration_stack.py:30. Eleven copies of a constant db/when.py:517 already exports as HOUR. db/when.py:503-509's entire comment is about this failure mode.
findings.fix: `from db.when import HOUR, DAY` in each, or re-export them from tests/staging.py.

findings.concept: a day in seconds, in a test fixture
findings.evidence: Declared at tests/test_a_camera_day_is_a_story.py:33, tests/test_every_file_has_a_when.py:32, tests/test_the_timeline_is_a_surface.py:31, tests/test_time_is_a_corroboration_stack.py:32 and (as 86_400.0) tests/test_empty_time_does_not_get_the_pixels.py:42 -- while tests/test_the_timeline_in_a_browser.py:22 binds the same name to an epoch. db/when.py:518 exports DAY.
findings.fix: `from db.when import DAY`.

findings.concept: the fixture's anchor instant, 2023-06-10 00:00 UTC
findings.evidence: Declared with the identical comment at tests/test_a_shelf_says_when.py:22, tests/test_every_file_has_a_when.py:33 and tests/test_the_timeline_is_a_surface.py:32; typed bare at tests/test_a_picture_has_a_place.py:169, tests/test_the_timeline_window_in_a_browser.py:26 and tests/test_the_timeline_window_in_a_browser.py:66; and bound to the wrong name at tests/test_the_timeline_in_a_browser.py:22. Six modules, four spellings, one instant.
findings.fix: One JUNE_10 in tests/staging.py, imported everywhere; delete the three bare literals and rename the DAY binding.

findings.concept: how many hex characters of a content hash a message shows
findings.evidence: Instances: sg_web/app.py:1244, sg_web/app.py:1250, sg_web/app.py:1262, db/runner.py:202. Four user-facing messages abbreviating a sha to the same width by hand. Low because the value is cosmetic; it is still four copies of one decision.
findings.fix: `short_sha(sha)` in db/naming.py, used by all four.

findings.concept: one day before now, for the settled-jobs count
findings.evidence: The 24 hours is also encoded in the result key on db/inspecting.py:166 (`settled_24h`), so the window is stated twice in two notations and neither derives from db/when.py:518 DAY.
findings.fix: `now - when.DAY`, and name the window (`SETTLED_WINDOW = when.DAY`) so the key and the arithmetic move together.

findings.concept: the ledger page the console asks for
findings.evidence: db/ledger.py:59 declares PAGE_MOST = 2_000 as the server's ceiling and clamps to it at db/ledger.py:137, db/ledger.py:145 and db/inspecting.py:342. The client asks for exactly the ceiling by retyping it, so lowering PAGE_MOST leaves the console silently truncating pages it believes are complete.
findings.fix: Expose PAGE_MOST through the generated contract and read it, or ask for a named client-side page size provably <= the server's.

findings.concept: the narrowest window the timeline opens on
findings.evidence: sg_web/timeline_view.py:221 declares `NARROWEST = 3_600` for the same surface and enforces it server-side at sg_web/timeline_view.py:983-984. The client retypes it and applies it at frontend/src/timeline.ts:393 and frontend/src/timeline.ts:548. Nothing holds the two together; a server that widens its floor gets client drags it will silently clamp.
findings.fix: Emit NARROWEST in the timeline view's payload (which already ships bin_seconds and the extent) and read it here.

findings.concept: the SVG viewBox width the bars are drawn in
findings.evidence: sg_web/timeline_view.py:224 declares `_W = 1000` as "The drawing's width in its own units (the SVG viewBox)". frontend/src/timeline.ts:112-118's own comment says the client inverts the axis 'exactly as the server drew it' -- and then retypes the width the server drew it at. Every click, drag and pan maps through this number.
findings.fix: Ship the viewBox width in the payload, or read it off the rendered `<svg viewBox>`, and delete the constant.

findings.concept: the first visit's window
findings.evidence: 86_400 typed rather than when.DAY, in a module whose sibling db/pages.py:1333-1340 multiplies every bin width from db/when.py precisely so this cannot drift (db/pages.py:1328-1332 records why). The same raw 86_400 recurs at sg_web/timeline_view.py:209 (four times), 213-216, 402-404, 443, 446, 465-468, 644-646, 657, 860, 865 and 875.
findings.fix: `from db import when`; write `30 * when.DAY` and replace the other raw 86_400 / 3_600 in this module with when.DAY / when.HOUR or with pages.BINS entries.

findings.concept: the window presets
findings.evidence: '1m' is 30 days and '1y' is 365 days here, while db/pages.py:1335 makes a month int(when.MONTH) (30.44 d) and db/pages.py:1334 makes a year int(when.YEAR) (365.2425 d). The preset labelled '1y' therefore selects a window narrower than the year bin the same page draws.
findings.fix: `("1w", 7 * when.DAY), ("1m", when.MONTH), ("3m", 3 * when.MONTH), ("1y", when.YEAR)`.

findings.concept: minutes to seconds
findings.evidence: The bare 60.0 conversion is typed three times -- db/events.py:213, db/events.py:229, db/events.py:248 -- in a package that exports db/when.py:516 MINUTE for exactly this. Low: the value cannot plausibly be wrong. It is still three untethered copies of a unit conversion in the module that decides session boundaries.
findings.fix: `* when.MINUTE`.

findings.concept: the epoch offset of the first Monday
findings.evidence: 345_600 is 4 * 86400 -- the epoch fell on a Thursday -- but it is typed flat in the one module that otherwise derives every span from db/when.py (db/pages.py:1333-1340), and nothing on the line states the derivation. Arguable: the value is correct and stable. It is still the only untethered number in a table whose comment (db/pages.py:1328-1332) exists because untethered numbers disagreed.
findings.fix: `MONDAY = 4 * int(when.DAY)  # the epoch was a Thursday`.

findings.concept: the preview variant's edge, restated in a docstring
findings.evidence: vision/thumbs.py:45 declares `EDGES = {"thumb": 512, "preview": 1440}` as the source. The numbers are restated in prose at sg_web/app.py:1267 (512), sg_web/app.py:1273 (1440) and db/oriented.py:123 ('at 1440 serves both the preview and the 512 thumb'). Low: prose cannot break a caller. It can and does go stale, and these are the surfaces a reader checks first.
findings.fix: Say 'longest side `thumbs.EDGES["preview"]`', or drop the number and point at vision/thumbs.py:45.

findings.concept: the kinds with no pixels
findings.evidence: The complement of vision/thumbs.py:53 PICTURED within db/facets.py:29 KINDS, typed out rather than computed. A sixth kind added to KINDS is in neither set, and the assertions at tests/test_the_walk_crosses_every_kind.py:196, 203, 219 and 265 quietly stop covering it. Not an oracle literal -- it is the set the test partitions by, not an expected answer.
findings.fix: `UNPICTURED = set(facets.KINDS) - set(thumbs.PICTURED)`.

findings.concept: the sanity cap on IFD entry count
findings.evidence: A decision literal in a parser reading attacker-supplied bytes (`if n > 4096: return {}`), with no comment deriving it -- in a function whose docstring (db/capture.py:441-442) is otherwise explicit that structural problems are 'absence, not an error'. A TIFF IFD's entry count is a uint16, so the format's own ceiling is 65535; 4096 is a policy, and it is unstated.
findings.fix: `_MOST_IFD_ENTRIES = 4096` at module scope with the sentence that justifies refusing an IFD larger than that.

findings.concept: how many day rows the timeline asks for
findings.evidence: A bare default on a public query function, with no comment deriving 400 and no constant. It collides numerically with db/resultset.py:164 MAX_PAGE_SIZE = 400 while denoting something else entirely, so a reader cannot tell whether the two are related. Its sibling db/pages.py:1658 uses 200 with the same silence.
findings.fix: Name it beside the other timeline bounds this module already names (db/pages.py:1347 SAMPLED_BINS_MOST, db/pages.py:1348 SAMPLES_PER_BIN): `TIMELINE_DAYS_MOST = 400`, with the sentence that justifies it.

findings.concept: how many session rows the timeline asks for
findings.evidence: Bare default, no derivation. sg_web/timeline_view.py:203 names the same quantity on the view side -- `SESSIONS_MOST = 200` -- with a full paragraph of justification at sg_web/timeline_view.py:199-202. The number the comment explains is on the other side of the seam from the number that actually bounds the query.
findings.fix: `TIMELINE_EVENTS_MOST = 200` in db/pages.py, and have sg_web/timeline_view.py:203 read it instead of restating it.

findings.concept: how many place names one read returns
findings.evidence: A five-thousand-row bare default with no comment. The same literal appears for unrelated reasons at db/connect.py:176 (busy_timeout ms), db/migrate.py:298, db/resultset.py:1260 and db/sample.py:38 -- where it IS named (MOST) and justified at db/sample.py:36-37.
findings.fix: `PLACES_MOST = 5_000` with the argument for 5000, matching the style db/sample.py:36-38 already uses.

findings.concept: the axis tick ladder
findings.evidence: A five-row table of raw seconds spanning sg_web/timeline_view.py:400-404, with no comment on any row and no derivation from db/when.py or db/pages.py BINS -- in a module that names and justifies its other ladders (sg_web/timeline_view.py:211-212 for _ZOOM, sg_web/timeline_view.py:205-206 for OPENING).
findings.fix: Build the rows from when.HOUR / when.DAY (`(when.HOUR, 5 * when.MINUTE), (6 * when.HOUR, 30 * when.MINUTE), ...`) and add the one line saying what a tick step is for.

findings.concept: the span above which the axis labels months instead of days
findings.evidence: 183 days is half a Julian year, but nothing says so, and the same `183 * 86_400` is the day-bin ceiling at sg_web/timeline_view.py:216 -- one number doing two jobs in one module, typed twice. Neither derives from db/when.py.
findings.fix: `HALF_YEAR = when.YEAR / 2` (or a named MONTH_LABELS_ABOVE), used at both sites.

findings.concept: the span above which only years are labelled
findings.evidence: 366 is a leap year in days, hand-typed, in the module that already disagrees with db/when.py:521 at lines 217-218 and 663. The comment at sg_web/timeline_view.py:444-445 explains the LABEL policy and never the number. sg_web/timeline_view.py:875 uses `2 * 366 * 86_400` for a different threshold with the same untethered 366.
findings.fix: `3 * when.YEAR` and `2 * when.YEAR`; delete both 366s.

findings.concept: the widest window that draws month sheets
findings.evidence: Named, but built from an untethered 366-day year -- the same hand-typed leap year as sg_web/timeline_view.py:446 -- while db/pages.py:1334 derives the year bin from when.YEAR. The threshold that chooses the calendar body and the bins that fill it come from two different years.
findings.fix: `SHEETS_WIDEST = 2 * when.YEAR`.

findings.concept: the floor below which the git sweep declares itself blind
findings.evidence: A decision literal in a linter rule (SG800) with no derivation, in a package whose policy module names every other threshold and justifies it -- sglint/policy.py:360 PAGE_QUERIES_MINIMUM = 12, sglint/policy.py:497 TEMPLATE_MINIMUM = 30, sglint/policy.py:498 SCRIPT_MINIMUM = 11, each with a comment above it. This rule's minimum is inline and silent.
findings.fix: Move it to sglint/policy.py as `TRACKED_MINIMUM: int = 100` with the same comment discipline as its neighbours.

findings.concept: the floor below which the line-ending parse declares itself broken
findings.evidence: Two more unnamed thresholds in one condition, again raising SG800. Same divergence from sglint/policy.py:360/497/498, which name and justify every minimum they own.
findings.fix: `ENDINGS_MINIMUM: int = 100` and `LF_MINIMUM: int = 50` in sglint/policy.py, each with the sentence that fixes it.

findings.concept: how many leading bytes are searched for the Canon CNDA thumbnail
findings.evidence: The docstring (db/capture.py:625-628) says the atom 'sits near the start of the file' and that 'the first `limit` bytes are searched' -- it explains the mechanism and never why four megabytes. Reading four MB per Canon MOV is a real cost decision left unstated.
findings.fix: `_CNDA_SEARCH_BYTES = 4_000_000` with the measurement or the spec fact that fixes it.

findings.concept: how long the WAL conversion waits for the exclusive lock
findings.evidence: The docstring (db/connect.py:62-68) explains at length WHY the wait exists and never why five seconds. The same duration appears in different units in the same module as `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000` (db/connect.py:176), with no stated link.
findings.fix: `LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS = 5.0` and `PRAGMA busy_timeout={int(LOCK_WAIT_SECONDS * 1000)}`, so the two cannot drift apart.

findings.concept: how many annotation search hits one read returns
findings.evidence: Bare default on an FTS query, no comment. Same value as db/resultset.py:163 DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE and db/pages.py:1809 with no stated relationship.
findings.fix: Read resultset.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE, or name it locally with the reason.

findings.concept: how many settled jobs the matrix shows
findings.evidence: Bare default; the sibling on the next function (db/inspecting.py:249, recent_events = 50) is another. Neither is named nor derived, and sg_web/activity.py:41 names a third quantity of the same shape (RECENT = 12) with a one-line justification -- so naming these is already the convention.
findings.fix: `MATRIX_RECENT = 30` and `JOB_RECENT_EVENTS = 50` at the top of db/inspecting.py beside TERMINAL.

findings.concept: how many ledger events a job detail carries
findings.evidence: Bare default, used as a slice bound at db/inspecting.py:338 (`history[-recent_events:]`). No derivation.
findings.fix: Name it (see db/inspecting.py:236).

findings.concept: how many job items one page returns
findings.evidence: Bare default; the clamp nine lines later (db/inspecting.py:375) uses a different unnamed literal (2_000, itself a copy of ledger.PAGE_MOST). A page default and a page ceiling, neither named.
findings.fix: `ITEMS_PAGE = 200` beside the ledger constants; clamp with ledger.PAGE_MOST.

findings.concept: how many settled jobs the cold list carries
findings.evidence: Bare default. sg_web/activity.py:41 declares `RECENT = 12` with the comment 'How many settled jobs the cold list carries beside the active ones' -- the justification for THIS number lives in another package, and the two are not linked.
findings.fix: Move RECENT into db/jobs.py beside the function it bounds and have sg_web/activity.py import it.

findings.concept: how many faces a run comparison lists
findings.evidence: Bare default, no comment -- twenty lines below db/pages.py:719, where the sibling bound DISAGREEMENTS_SHOWN = 50 is named and given a four-line justification (db/pages.py:713-718). Two bounds on the same comparison surface, one explained and one not.
findings.fix: `FACES_ACROSS_RUNS_SHOWN = 20` beside DISAGREEMENTS_SHOWN.

findings.concept: how many stories the shelf lists
findings.evidence: Bare default. 60 is also db/resultset.py:163 DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE and db/derived.py:1526's annotation-search default -- three page sizes of 60, one named.
findings.fix: Read `resultset.DEFAULT_PAGE_SIZE` if it is the same decision; otherwise name `STORIES_MOST = 60` and say why it differs.

findings.concept: how many neighbours a filmstrip shows
findings.evidence: Bare default on a public function, nine lines under `NEIGHBORHOOD_MOST = 51` (db/resultset.py:1205), which IS named. The ceiling is named, the default is not, and 15 vs 51 has no stated relationship.
findings.fix: `NEIGHBORHOOD_DEFAULT = 15` beside NEIGHBORHOOD_MOST, with the relationship stated.

findings.concept: the debounce before the console re-renders, in milliseconds
findings.evidence: A bare `}, 400);` with no name, while the same file names every other bound it owns (frontend/src/operations.ts:35, frontend/src/operations.ts:36) and frontend/src/reread.ts:20 names the same order of magnitude as POLL_MS = 400.
findings.fix: `const RENDER_DEBOUNCE_MS = 400;` at the top of the IIFE beside the other named constants.

findings.concept: the reconnect delay after the job feed closes, in milliseconds
findings.evidence: `feed.onclose = () => window.setTimeout(open, 2000);` -- a fixed reconnect backoff with no name and no comment, on the socket sg_web/app.py:1416-1425 closes with code 1011 expecting the client to come back. The server's side of that contract is documented at sg_web/app.py:1416-1421; the client's delay is not.
findings.fix: `const RECONNECT_MS = 2000;` with a line pointing at the sg_web/app.py:1416 close-code contract.

findings.concept: the cap on tiles requested for one bin
findings.evidence: A bare cap inside a computation, no name and no comment. 400 is also db/resultset.py:164 MAX_PAGE_SIZE and db/pages.py:1652's day limit; a reader cannot tell whether this is the same bound reaching the client or a coincidence.
findings.fix: `const TILES_MOST = 400;` and a line saying whether it tracks the server's MAX_PAGE_SIZE.

findings.concept: the row-height bounds for the pictures strip
findings.evidence: Three unexplained pixel bounds in one object literal, only the storage key named. The comment above (frontend/src/timeline.ts:813-815) explains the INTERACTION and none of the numbers.
findings.fix: Keep the object but state in one line what fixes 120 and 520 (the thumbnail edge from vision/thumbs.py:45, or a measured layout bound).

findings.concept: how long a git subprocess may run
findings.evidence: Bare keyword on the process boundary every rule in the module goes through, with no comment. Fifteen minutes for `git ls-files` is a policy nobody stated.
findings.fix: `GIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900` in sglint/policy.py with the reason.

findings.concept: how much of a failed checkout's stderr the finding carries
findings.evidence: An unexplained slice bound in a diagnostic message. Truncating the only evidence a failure produces is a decision; 200 is not derived.
findings.fix: `_STDERR_SHOWN = 200` with the reason, or carry the whole stderr.

findings.concept: the detector-confidence floor
findings.evidence: Declared as a bare default twice -- vision/faces.py:225 (OpenCVFaceBackend) and vision/faces.py:412 (InsightFaceBackend). The docstrings explain what the knob MEANS (vision/faces.py:232-236, vision/faces.py:418-420) and, for min_face_px and detect_max_side, cite measurements; 0.5 itself is derived nowhere, and two backends carrying it independently means changing the operating point takes two edits. Arguable: two sites, not three.
findings.fix: `DEFAULT_MIN_DET_SCORE = 0.5` at module scope beside vision/faces.py:143's `_SIM_CHUNK_SIZE`, referenced by both constructors.

findings.concept: the noise-floor face size
findings.evidence: Same shape: bare default at vision/faces.py:226 and vision/faces.py:413. The reason is written out at vision/faces.py:234-236 but attached to only one of the two copies; vision/faces.py:419-420 restates it in different words.
findings.fix: `DEFAULT_MIN_FACE_PX = 24` at module scope with the single justification, referenced by both.
